question: What is the main goal of using an Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: To share patient health information across multiple clinics and hospitals
options.B: To store private insurance company financial statements
options.C: To track hospital staff attendance and monthly salaries
options.D: To replace physical nursing textbooks in the library

explanation: You got this! EHRs are designed to let different healthcare providers share patient info safely so everyone is on the same page. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why do we call an EHR a 'single source of truth' for the healthcare team?

options.A: Because all authorized workers see the exact same up-to-date patient info
options.B: Because test results change automatically to match the doctor's opinion
options.C: Because paper charts are completely outlawed in Nigeria
options.D: Because patients write their own diagnoses into the computer

explanation: Spot on! Having one digital record stops confusion because every nurse and doctor views the exact same current clinical details. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which EHR tool allows doctors and nurses to type in medication and treatment orders digitally?
explanation: Great job! CPOE is just the digital system used to send patient care orders straight to the pharmacy and other departments. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: How do clinical decision support tools help you as a nurse during drug administration?

options.A: By sending automated warnings about drug allergies or abnormal vitals
options.B: By calculating your monthly salary and allowances
options.C: By locking the screen whenever blood pressure rises
options.D: By printing paper copies of every single prescription

explanation: You're learning fast! These smart alerts act like a safety net, warning you immediately if a patient has a known allergy or dangerous vitals. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main difference between an EMR (Electronic Medical Record) and an EHR?

options.A: An EMR costs millions, while an EHR is completely free
options.B: An EHR shares data across multiple facilities, while an EMR stays in one clinic
options.C: An EHR is only for pharmacists, while an EMR is for student nurses
options.D: An EMR is on paper, while an EHR is on a flash drive

explanation: Exactly! Think of an EMR as staying inside one single clinic, while an EHR can travel and share data across different hospitals. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: A patient moves from a primary health clinic to a big teaching hospital. Which system is best for viewing their full past medical history?
explanation: You nailed it! EHRs are built for tracking patient history across different healthcare institutions over time. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h3)

question: What common headache in clinical practice do EHRs instantly fix?

options.A: Shortages of sterile syringes in the ward
options.B: Delays in patients arriving from rural villages
options.C: The need to measure patient vital signs every shift
options.D: Trying to read terrible handwriting on medication charts

explanation: Too true! Digital typing gets rid of messy handwriting, which stops dangerous medication mix-ups before they happen. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: If a nurse spends less time digging through filing cabinets and more time comforting patients, what EHR benefit does this show?

options.B: Improved efficiency and faster data retrieval
options.C: Automatic diagnosis of complex surgical diseases
options.D: Guaranteed promotion to senior nursing officer

explanation: Brilliant! Digital systems make finding info quick and easy, giving you more precious time for actual bedside nursing. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is a major headache for using EHRs in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: A complete lack of sick patients needing beds
options.B: Too much high-speed fiber internet everywhere
options.C: Total bans on computer usage in clinical wards
options.D: Frequent power outages and unstable electricity

explanation: Spot on! Unreliable power is a real challenge for keeping computers and digital records running smoothly without backup generators. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why might experienced nurses sometimes resist when a hospital first brings in an EHR system?

options.A: They are comfortable and used to long-time paper charting habits
options.B: They are legally forbidden from touching computer keyboards
options.C: They love spending hours searching for lost paper files
options.D: They know digital records cannot store vital signs

explanation: Understandable, right? Change is hard, and sticking to what you've known for years is normal, but staff adapt with good training! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which practice represents a serious breach of EHR security by a nurse?

options.A: Logging out of the terminal when leaving the ward
options.B: Checking lab results for an assigned patient on duty
options.C: Sharing personal login passwords with a colleague
options.D: Reading hospital confidentiality policies during orientation

explanation: Password sharing compromises accountability and violates security protocols, allowing unauthorized users to access sensitive patient files under another clinician's identity. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main reason hospitals use 'role-based access control' in their EHR systems?

options.A: To stop patients from ever seeing their lab results
options.B: To restrict staff to viewing only the patient data needed for their job
options.C: To make computer screens turn off automatically at night
options.D: To ensure every doctor and nurse earns the exact same salary

explanation: Spot on! This protects patient privacy by making sure staff only open files for the specific patients they are caring for. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h6)

question: How does blending predictive analytics with EHRs change modern nursing care?

options.A: From digital records back to manual paper exercise books
options.B: From bedside patient care to hospital financial auditing
options.C: From just reacting to problems to stopping them before they start
options.D: From teamwork back to isolated solo nursing practice

explanation: Amazing! Smart tools help nurses spot early warning signs and step in before a patient's condition gets worse. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h7)

question: Why is learning computer skills becoming just as important for student nurses as clinical skills?

options.A: Because modern hospitals rely heavily on electronic records and smart tools
options.B: Because physical thermometers and stethoscopes are banned
options.C: Because nurses will be forced to write computer programming software
options.D: Because paper charts are illegal to keep in private homes

explanation: You got it! As hospitals go digital, being comfortable with technology helps you document care and keep patients safe. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h7)
